_readme: Every permanent, account-wide Divine Principality upgrade. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id is written into save data as a purchase (SaveData.purchasedUpgradeIds), so NEVER rename one after a save exists -- a save drops any purchase whose id no longer resolves, so a rename reads to the player as a refund they did not ask for. UpgradeEntryResolver refuses a duplicate id, a missing displayName, a negative cost and a negative startingGoldBonus at build time, and nothing is written for the whole type when any row fails, because a catalogue that merely lost a row is the quietest possible failure. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM TALENTS: talents are per-character build power bought with a run's own progression, these are profile-wide and bought with Principality currency, so the two never compete for the same pot. SHOP ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that would silently reshuffle the shop (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). TWO ROWS TODAY, and what each one is for. extra_recruit_slot is the only upgrade any code names by id -- SaveData.ExtraRecruitSlotUpgradeId -- and it raises the squad size by one, which is what makes the fourth character in characters.json reachable at all; renaming it breaks that constant and the resolver cannot see the constant, so this is the one id to leave alone. starting_gold_boost is the only user of startingGoldBonus and the field exists for it: an upgrade grants in-run currency at the start of every run through that number rather than through a case in code, so a second gold upgrade is a row and not a branch. Costs are first-pass and unbalanced -- there is no Principality shop screen yet, so nothing has ever charged anybody 50 for anything. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.

upgrades.description: Bring an additional character on every run.
Begin each run with extra gold.
